finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 15-23 contain a fenced Markdown diagram of the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle, not Ruby backtick execution or shell syntax. There is no executable command or instruction to run a command.
Line 43 is an example test name for invalid data handling. It does not request system information, host inspection, or reconnaissance.
Lines 31-33 describe writing only enough code to pass a test. They contain no network probing, external requests, or discovery behavior.

content.value_statement: Developers often skip tests or write them after implementation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through red-green-refactor discipline.
actual_capabilities: Lists the three laws of test-driven development.
Defines practical rules for RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR phases.
Shows how to structure tests with Arrange, Act, and Assert.
Prioritizes happy path, error case, edge case, and performance tests.
Describes a simple multi-agent pattern for AI-assisted TDD.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or test framework integrations.
Does not generate language-specific fixtures without project context.
Requires clear requirements before useful tests can be written.
Provides workflow guidance, not guaranteed test correctness.

use_cases.title: Start a New Feature
use_cases.description: Guide the first failing test, minimal implementation, and cleanup steps for a new behavior.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Write a failing test that reproduces a bug before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Coordinate AI Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Assign separate agents to test writing, implementation, and refactoring while preserving TDD order.

prompt_templates.title: Begin a TDD Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill. Help me define one failing test for this requirement before any implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill. List the happy path, error case, and edge case tests for this feature in priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Run Red Green Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill. Walk me through RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR steps for this change, and stop after each phase.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Multi-Agent TDD
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill. Split this work across a test-writing agent, an implementation agent, and a refactoring agent.

output_examples.input: Add email validation to a signup form.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes failing tests for valid addresses, malformed addresses, and empty input. It then suggests minimal implementation and refactoring checks.

output_examples.input: Fix a bug where discounts apply twice.
output_examples.output: The assistant starts with a regression test that captures the duplicate discount. It then limits implementation to the smallest passing change.
The assistant verifies tests are green, identifies duplication and naming issues, and recommends small refactoring steps without changing behavior.

best_practices: Write the failing test before changing production code.
Keep each test focused on one observable behavior.
Refactor only after the full test suite passes.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation first and adding tests later.
Testing private implementation details instead of behavior.
Expanding scope during the GREEN phase.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant follow test-driven development using RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR steps.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. The user or agent must run the project test command.

faq.question: Can it work with any programming language?
faq.answer: Yes, the workflow is language independent when the user provides project context and test framework details.

faq.question: Is it useful for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages writing a failing regression test before changing the code.

faq.question: Does it replace test design judgment?
faq.answer: No. It structures the process, but users still need clear requirements and meaningful assertions.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
